description: This case study is a paper presented at the 1999 USCID workshop on modernization of irrigation water delivery systems, describing how the Irrigation Training and Research Center at Cal Poly worked with the Patterson Irrigation District, partly funded by the US Bureau of Reclamation Mid-Pacific Region, to modernize its facilities. The district lies in the San Joaquin Valley and pumps mostly from the San Joaquin River through a series of pump stations and canal pools that lift water to lateral canals laid on the contour. Modernization to date included discussions with the district board, unsteady flow simulation of the first main canal pool, a new SCADA system, a large Replogle flume, remote monitoring of water levels, downstream control of the canal, variable frequency drives on pump stations, and flow control and measurement designs at the heads of lateral canals. The paper gives guidelines and components for a phased approach. Coverage: one district, with design steps, not measured results. Access: the abstract page is free; the full text was not opened, and the licence is not stated. Caveats: the results are expected benefits, not verified savings, and the paper dates from 1999. It informs canal automation and pump scheduling simulation and optimisation, and relates to the Central California Irrigation District modernisation case already catalogued.
